children: Metcash is playing defense with its A$80 million-A$85 million acquisition of Peries Group, which owns 15 IGA supermarkets in Australia's Queensland state, suggest Jefferies. Metcash likely wanted to prevent sales leaving the IGA network to a competitor, analyst Michael Simotas says. Peries's supermarkets generated around A$264 million in retail sales in FY26. Metcash said its wholesale sales to Peries were A$150 million in the same year. "Metcash may not be the long-term owner and we see strong potential for divestment of some or all stores to existing IGA operators, noting they appear a good fit for Metcash's large Queensland JV partner," Jefferies says. It retains a buy call and A$3.40/share price target on Metcash, which ended Monday at A$3.16. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
